subject: Air-bridge standby manifest & seat-priority for Bayview exec workshop
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bayview workshop — immediate: overnight connection with VIP arrival (hold seats)

Team,

Quick heads-up: BrightSpark confirmed an inbound group for our Bayview workshop arriving the evening of 4/20. One of their execs (CISO) is on a red-eye that currently routes through LAX with a ~45-minute connection to SFO — that’s a hard no for us. We need a resilient swap plan that keeps the delegation together and preserves the shared shuttle window (pickup at 08:30 on 4/21).

Requests:
- Laura: can you pull up alternate routings that avoid LAX tight-connection legs and prioritize through-ticketed itineraries? Prefer same-carrier where possible.
- Tessa: hold 3x seats in the Bayview shuttle (van), mark them as PRIORITY for the arriving CISO and two IT leads; vendor shuttle vendor needs PAX count by 4/19 EOD.
- Dev: if we need to upgrade a leg for swap resiliency (to secure confirmed seats on the earlier flight), outline the estimated upcharge so we can pre-approve.

Attached the latest workshop manifest (names masked for calendar privacy) — highlighted rows are the execs to prioritize. I’ll loop in BrightSpark once we have a firm routing recommendation.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122
Redwood Inference

Attachments: workshop_manifest.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bayview workshop — immediate: overnight connection with VIP arrival (hold seats)

Marcus —

I ran three routing options and annotated tradeoffs in the attached PDF (short summary below):

Option A — Preferred (no LAX): SFO -> SEA -> direct to OAK (same alliance through ticket)
- Pros: longer connection buffer (90+ min), same alliance = easier reissues
- Cons: +$65 per pax on average vs current routing

Option B — Upgrade current routing (earlier LAX leg + confirmed seats)
- Pros: minimal itinerary change for most attendees
- Cons: still passes LAX; if inbound delayed by >60 min we risk miss

Option C — Alternate carrier nonstop into SFO (higher cost, better reliability)
- Pros: best chance to keep the group together; seat assignment flexibility
- Cons: ~2–3x cost of Option A for some pax, limited inventory for group of 8

Recommendation: go with Option A for the execs (CISO + IT leads) and hold Option C as a fallback for the remainder of the delegation. If Dev can confirm upcharge approvals, I’ll place temporary holds and start the reissue process.

I’ve tentatively held 4 seats on the Option A routing (hold expires 4/18 18:00 PST). Shuttle vendor is on standby for the 08:30 window pending final PAX list. See attached: proposed-itinerary-v2.pdf.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Programs Lead, Events | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-itinerary-v2.pdf (15 pages)

From: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@brightspark.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 18:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bayview workshop — immediate: overnight connection with VIP arrival (hold seats)

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Our CISO’s original flight (red-eye) just got pushed by their travel team — they’ll actually now land SFO at 06:50 on 4/21 (no LAX connection) which is better for the shuttle window, but two of the IT leads are still on the LAX tight-connection routing. Can we prioritize getting those two on the Option A routing you recommended? If there’s a small upcharge, BrightSpark will cover it — we just need the group together on arrival.

Two asks from our side:
- please confirm shuttle pickup point (we prefer Door 4 at SFO arrivals) and an ETA buffer for a later CISO arrival if they miss the 06:50 shuttle;
- can you provide the PNRs once reissues are completed so our travel desk can sync?

Appreciate the responsiveness — we want a smooth check-in at the venue.

Best,
Morgan Blake
Director, Partnerships | BrightSpark
morgan.blake@brightspark.com
+1 617-555-3388

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@brightspark.com>, FlyWest Ops <ops@flywest.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 07:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bayview workshop — immediate: overnight connection with VIP arrival (hold seats)

Team — final update below and action items completed:

What we did
- Swapped the two IT leads from their LAX-tight connection onto Option A via SEA (reissue performed with FlyWest). PNRs attached.
- Confirmed CISO will now arrive 06:50; shuttle vendor will pick at Door 4 SFO Arrivals. Vendor will hold a 20-minute buffer for late arrivals.
- Upcharges: BrightSpark will cover $142.80 total for the two reissues (Dev, please record as chargeback to DEAL-9821).

Attachments and PNRs
- swapped-pnr-stub.txt (3 small PNR stubs) — includes confirmation numbers and seat priority flags.

Next steps / owners
- Laura: send final PAX manifest (with full names) to the shuttle vendor by 4/21 10:00 PST.
- Tessa: print priority badge set for the three execs (CISO + 2 IT leads) and add a red ribbon on arrival bags.
- Dev: please log the cost in the deal ledger and email finance the chargeback code.
- Marcus: I’ll send a single email to BrightSpark with the consolidated PNRs and the ground pickup map.

Thanks everyone for moving fast. We should be set for the Bayview arrival and shuttle window barring any last-minute flight irregularities.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: swapped-pnr-stub.txt (text)
